items.title: Retail earnings dominate the week ahead
points: Home Depot reports Tuesday, a read on home improvement demand amid high borrowing costs and weak housing activity.
Target reports Wednesday, with focus on discretionary spending and second-half outlook.
Walmart reports Thursday having beaten estimates in 15 of the past 16 quarters; results should move Costco, Kroger and Albertsons.
TJX, Lowe's and Ross Stores also report Wednesday–Thursday, alongside Analog Devices and Estee Lauder.

items.title: Fed July minutes and manufacturing data
points: July Federal Reserve meeting minutes land Wednesday, with investors seeking detail on the rate debate after three hawkish dissents from Lorie Logan, Beth Hammack and Neel Kashkari (hawkish = favoring higher rates to fight inflation).
Empire State manufacturing index Monday and Philadelphia Fed manufacturing report Thursday give regional U.S. factory readings.
Global PMI (Purchasing Managers Index — a survey of business activity in manufacturing and services) reports Friday show international conditions.

items.title: Asian tech and equipment earnings
points: Baidu reports Tuesday and Alibaba Thursday, testing Chinese e-commerce and tech health amid regulatory pressure.
Deere reports Thursday, reflecting farm equipment demand.
Results come amid questions on China's recovery and tariff impacts on U.S. importers.

items.title: Index change and sports betting catalysts
points: Reddit joins the S&P 500 Tuesday, replacing AvalonBay Communities and triggering passive index fund buying.
Premier League season kicks off Friday, a revenue driver for DraftKings, Flutter Entertainment and MGM Resorts' BetMGM.

items.title: BridgeBio Pharma beats Q2
points: BridgeBio topped Q2 estimates by $24 million, with Attruby sales up 311% year-over-year to $222.4 million.
Company is on track for over $1 billion in combined 2026 sales.

items.title: Wendy's financial and operational crisis
points: Six straight quarters of same-store sales declines; U.S. same-restaurant sales fell 7% in Q2 2026 versus a 2.3% decline a year earlier.
Adjusted operating profit fell 13.2% year-over-year and 289 U.S. locations closed in the first half of 2026, out of roughly 5,700.
Balance sheet strained: $2.7 billion in long-term debt against $341 million in cash; the stock is down 65% over five years.
A dividend cut freed capital, but Bernstein notes net leverage at 5.0x sits at the top of the company's target range.
Billionaire Nelson Peltz is reportedly near a buyout deal for the second time this year, though CEO Bob Wright has yet to stabilize sales.

items.title: Why the brand may not be fixable
points: No signature sandwich to rival the Whopper or Big Mac; Wendy's is better known for baked potatoes than fries.
Pricing seen as too expensive as Burger King and McDonald's push higher quality and aggressive value menus.
No meaningful rewards program versus Chipotle, McDonald's or Starbucks, and the mobile app is an afterthought.
'Fresh beef' and the square burger no longer differentiate; breakfast has 'failed mightily' and may be dropped in 2027.
Many locations haven't been updated since 1987, delivery orders arrive sloppy, and GLP-1 medications (appetite-suppressing weight-loss drugs) threaten fast food demand broadly.

issues.subject: Morning Brief: 20 reasons why Wendy's may be doomed

headlines: Wendy's posted six straight quarters of same-store sales declines, with US sales down 7% in Q2 2026, as CEO Bob Wright struggles to reverse the struggling chain's trajectory.
Stock has fallen 65% over five years and 289 US locations closed in the first half of 2026, raising questions about the chain's long-term viability.
Billionaire Nelson Peltz is reportedly near a buyout deal for Wendy's for the second time this year, but the chain faces structural competitive disadvantages against McDonald's and Burger King.
Wendy's carries $2.7 billion in long-term debt versus only $341 million in cash, severely limiting management's ability to invest in turnaround efforts.

Executive Editor argues the 84-year-old brand lacks differentiation—no signature sandwich, weak mobile app, expensive pricing, and neglected restaurant locations—making a turnaround unlikely even under new ownership.

sections.title: 1. Wendy's Financial and Operational Crisis
points: Six consecutive quarters of same-store sales declines; US same-restaurant sales crashed 7% in Q2 2026 versus 2.3% decline year-over-year.
Adjusted operating profits tanked 13.2% year-over-year; 289 US locations closed in first half of 2026 out of approximately 5,700 total US Wendy's.
Balance sheet severely constrained with $2.7 billion in long-term debt against only $341 million in cash, leaving limited capital for turnaround investments.
Dividend cut freed up capital, but Bernstein analyst notes net leverage at 5.0x sits at top of company's target range, constraining deployment speed.

sections.title: 2. Competitive Disadvantages Against Rivals
points: Burger King and McDonald's are winning with higher-quality offerings and aggressive value menus, while Wendy's food pricing has become too expensive.
Wendy's lacks a meaningful rewards program comparable to Chipotle, McDonald's, or Starbucks; mobile app is considered an afterthought.
No signature sandwich comparable to Whopper or Big Mac; brand is better known for baked potatoes than french fries, undercutting core hamburger positioning.
McDonald's leads on beverage platform (coffee, energy drinks) and Taco Bell dominates late-night fast food—Wendy's is non-competitive in both segments.

sections.title: 3. Structural Brand and Consumer Perception Issues
points: Square burger and 'fresh beef' messaging no longer differentiate Wendy's in 2026; consumers expect fresh beef as standard from all fast food chains.
Breakfast initiative has 'failed mightily' and may be discontinued in 2027; Frosty dessert no longer drives customer traffic.
Delivery orders frequently arrive sloppy; many restaurant locations haven't been updated since 1987, while competitors aggressively modernized storefronts.

GLP-1 medications (drugs that suppress appetite for weight loss) are emerging threat to entire fast food industry; Wendy's lacks brand strength to weather this disruption compared to category leaders.
